triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina
triplets.tail: Argentina defaulted on approximately $103 billion in sovereign debt in December 2001

triplets.head: NML Capital
triplets.tail: Subsidiary of hedge fund Elliott Management — purchased Argentine bonds at deep discounts

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina
triplets.tail: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (Judge Thomas Griesa)

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina
triplets.tail: Approximately $2.4 billion

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina
triplets.tail: Judge Griesa ordered Argentina to make ratable payment to holdouts every time it paid restructured bondholders — upheld by Second Circuit 2013

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — Ghana (ARA Libertad)
triplets.tail: Ghanaian Commercial Court, Tema; then ITLOS

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — Ghana (ARA Libertad)
triplets.tail: Argentine Navy training frigate ARA Libertad

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — Ghana (ARA Libertad)
triplets.tail: October 2012 — court ordered seizure of warship

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — Ghana (ARA Libertad)
triplets.tail: 15 December 2012 — unanimously ordered Ghana to release vessel; warships enjoy absolute immunity under UNCLOS Article 32

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — France
triplets.tail: Argentine Embassy bank accounts in Paris

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — France
triplets.tail: French Cour de cassation

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — France
triplets.tail: Attachment denied — embassy bank accounts immune under customary international law

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — Belgium
triplets.tail: Blocked by Belgian anti-vulture fund law (2015); law upheld by Belgian Constitutional Court in 2018

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — U.S. (FRBNY)
triplets.tail: Argentine central bank reserves at Federal Reserve Bank of New York

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina — U.S. (FRBNY)
triplets.tail: Attachment rejected — central bank property immune under FSIA § 1611(b)(1)

triplets.head: Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd. (Supreme Court)
Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd. (Supreme Court)
triplets.tail: FSIA does not provide immunity from post-judgment discovery of foreign state's extraterritorial assets

triplets.head: Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd. (Supreme Court)
triplets.tail: 7–1 (Justice Scalia writing; Justice Ginsburg dissenting in part)

triplets.head: NML Capital v. Argentina
triplets.tail: Settlement in February 2016 under President Macri — approximately $4.65 billion paid to holdouts; Judge Griesa lifted injunctions

triplets.head: Argentina 2005/2010 debt restructuring
triplets.tail: Approximately 93% of bondholders accepted

triplets.head: Crystallex International Corp. v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: 2002 — exclusive rights to extract gold from Las Cristinas, one of world's largest gold deposits

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: 2011 — Venezuela revoked mining rights without compensation

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: April 2016 — approximately $1.2 billion plus interest

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia confirmed as U.S. judgment; D.C. Circuit affirmed

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: Alter ego / veil-piercing — argued PDVSA was alter ego of Venezuela

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: Shares in PDV Holding, Inc. (PDVH) — parent company of CITGO Petroleum

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela — Delaware District Court (2018)
triplets.tail: PDVSA is alter ego of Venezuela under Bancec factors — extensive day-to-day state control

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela — Third Circuit (July 2019)
triplets.tail: Affirmed alter ego finding and attachment of PDVH shares; property used for commercial activity under FSIA § 1610(a)(6)

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela — Third Circuit
triplets.tail: Treasury Department OFAC approval likely needed for any actual sale due to U.S. sanctions on Venezuela

triplets.head: Crystallex v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: Ongoing — sale process for CITGO shares being overseen by Delaware District Court; complicated by sanctions and competing creditors

triplets.head: ConocoPhillips v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: 2019 — approximately $8.7 billion for expropriation of Venezuelan oil projects

triplets.head: ConocoPhillips v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: Pursued in Netherlands (Curaçao) — attached PDVSA refinery assets on Curaçao and Bonaire; proceedings ongoing

triplets.head: Gold Reserve v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: 2014 — approximately $740 million for expropriation of gold mining rights

triplets.head: Gold Reserve v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: Pursued in France, Luxembourg, and U.S.; successfully attached Euroclear shares in France

triplets.head: Gold Reserve v. Venezuela
triplets.tail: Settlement in 2016 — payment through mining joint venture arrangement

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania
triplets.tail: December 2013 — approximately $250 million against Romania for abolishing tax incentives

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania
triplets.tail: 2015 — ruled payment of award constitutes illegal state aid under EU law; ordered Romania not to pay

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania — U.S.
triplets.tail: D.C. District Court and D.C. Circuit

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania — U.S.
triplets.tail: Award confirmed; Romania's EU state aid arguments rejected; sanctions imposed for non-payment

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania — UK
triplets.tail: UK Supreme Court (2020)

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania — UK
triplets.tail: Stay lifted; enforcement permitted — ICSID obligations not overridden by EU law

triplets.head: Micula v. Romania — EU
triplets.tail: Upheld Commission's state aid decision — direct conflict with ICSID obligations

triplets.head: Sedelmayer v. Russia
triplets.tail: Swedish Supreme Court

triplets.head: Sedelmayer v. Russia
triplets.tail: 1 July 2011

triplets.head: Sedelmayer v. Russia
triplets.tail: Building in central Stockholm owned by Russia, formerly used by Russian trade delegation — largely rented out commercially

triplets.head: Sedelmayer v. Russia
triplets.tail: Attachment permitted — building used for commercial purposes, therefore not immune from execution

triplets.head: AIG Capital Partners v. Kazakhstan (2005)
triplets.tail: English High Court

triplets.head: AIG Capital Partners v. Kazakhstan (2005)
triplets.tail: National Fund (sovereign wealth fund) account at London bank held by National Bank of Kazakhstan

triplets.head: AIG Capital Partners v. Kazakhstan (2005)
triplets.tail: Funds immune — central bank property cannot be regarded as in use for commercial purposes under UK SIA section 14(4)

triplets.head: LETCO v. Liberia (1987)
triplets.tail: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia

triplets.head: LETCO v. Liberia (1987)
triplets.tail: One of earliest ICSID enforcement cases; confirmed ICSID member states waived jurisdictional immunity; execution difficult due to lack of Liberian commercial assets in U.S.

triplets.head: Bancec factors
triplets.tail: First National City Bank v. Banco Para El Comercio Exterior de Cuba, 462 U.S. 611 (1983)

triplets.head: Bancec factors
triplets.tail: Test for piercing corporate veil between foreign state and its instrumentalities/state-owned enterprises

triplets.head: Propend Finance v. Sing (1997)
triplets.tail: UK Court of Appeal

triplets.head: Propend Finance v. Sing (1997)
triplets.tail: UK SIA Section 14(1) extends immunity to individual employees or officers of a foreign state acting as organs or agents in exercise of sovereign authority

triplets.head: Jones v. Saudi Arabia (2006)
triplets.tail: Foreign state entitled to claim immunity for its servants as it could if sued itself — immunity cannot be circumvented by suing servants or agents

triplets.head: Samantar v. Yousuf (U.S. Supreme Court, 2010)
triplets.tail: FSIA does not govern immunity of individual foreign officials — their immunity determined by common law

triplets.head: Benkharbouche v. Secretary of State (UK Supreme Court, 2017)
triplets.tail: UK SIA had been based on erroneous view of international law that warranted broader immunity than customary law required, particularly in employment cases

triplets.head: UK SIA Section 16(4)
triplets.tail: Part I (jurisdictional immunity) does not apply to criminal proceedings
